'''''Instantons and Four-Manifolds''''' is a mathematical [[textbook]] about [[Yang–Mills theory]], or more generally [[gauge theory]], and its application to the study of the geometry and topology of [[Smooth manifold|smooth]] [[4-manifold|4-manifolds]] as described by [[Donaldson theory]]. It is considered a standard work for this topic.<ref name=":0">{{citation|author=[[Ronald J. Stern]] |date=1986-03-14 |doi=10.1126/science.231.4743.1316 |pages=1316-1317 |periodical=Mathematical Sciences Research Institute Publications |title=Four-dimensional topology |volume=231}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> It was written by [[Daniel Freed]] and [[Karen Uhlenbeck]], who received the [[Abel Prize]] in 2019 for her work in the field.<ref name="citation">{{cite web|title=2019: Karen Keskulla Uhlenbeck|publisher=The Abel Prize|url=https://abelprize.no/abel-prize-laureates/2019|access-date=2022-07-22}}</ref> It was published in 1984 with a second revised edition in 1991.

== Content ==

''Instantons and Four-Manifolds'' begins with a dense collection of the most important constructions and results of the field, which are about the [[intersection form]] and [[Signature (topology)|signature]] as well as [[Smooth structure|smooth structures]] and [[Donaldson invariant|Donaldson invariants]]. Afterwards, 4-manifolds are examined closer under the topological and smooth perspective as well as the [[Yang–Mills equations]] from mathematical perspective.<ref>Freed & Uhlenbeck 84, Kapitel 1 und 2</ref> In the rest of the textbook, the works of [[Simon Donaldson]] about the [[Yang–Mills moduli space#Self-dual SU(2) moduli space|self-dual SU(2) Yang–Mills moduli space]] and [[Donaldson's theorem]], which earned him a [[Fields Medal]] in 1986,<ref name=":4">{{cite web|access-date=2026-01-25 |title=Fields Medals 1986 - Donaldson, Faltings, Freedman Achievements |url=https://www.mathunion.org/imu-awards/fields-medal/fields-medals-1986}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> [[Clifford Taubes]] about Taubes' theorem as well as [[Ron Fintushel]] and [[Ronald J. Stern]] about the [[Yang–Mills moduli space#Self-dual SO(3) moduli space|self-dual SO(3) Yang–Mills moduli space]] are explained.<ref>Freed & Uhlenbeck 84, Chapter 4, 6, 7 und 10</ref>

== Background ==

After the publication of Donaldson's theorem, Karen Uhlenbeck and Michael Freedman, who just like Simon Donaldson was awarded the Fields Medal in 1986 for his contributions,<ref name=":4" /> gave a seminar to rigorously work through it. Daniel Freed was responsible for taking notes. Although the seminar was well visited, within three months there was no significant progress in understanding, which caused the development of a textbook. ("Unfortnutely, we found after three months that we had covered most of the published material but had made little progress toward giving a complete, detailed proof."<ref name=":52">Freed & Uhlenbeck 84, Preface to the first edition</ref>) Central were all analytical considerations, which are the core of Donaldson's original publications, but aren't described in deep details. ("The seminar bogged down in the hard analysis, which also takes up most of Donaldson's paper (in less detail)."<ref name=":52" />)

== Reviews ==

[[Ronald J. Stern]] wrote, "this book exposes the beautiful confluence of deep techniques and ideas from mathematical physics and the topological study of the differential study of compact four-dimensional manifolds". Furthermore, "this work is in sharp contrast to the earlier [[Freedman classification|remarkable results of Michael Freedman]]".<ref name=":0" />

Thomas Parker wrote, the textbook "is a timely and detailled exposition of perhaps the most remarkable product of this [between physics and differential geometry] interaction".<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Parker |first=Thomas |title=Instantons and Four-Manifolds (Daniel S. Freed and Karen K. Uhlenbeck) |url=https://epubs.siam.org/doi/pdf/10.1137/1029032 |journal=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics (SIAM) |pages=160-162 |doi=10.1137/1029032|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
